reviewDecisions.rationale: Record heavy-truck demand has direct listed-company transmission and can be tested against contemporaneous valuation and price absorption.
Electronics profit resilience is real, but premium expectations and the distinction between company growth and server-DRAM exposure require deep separation.
The memory cycle is still positive but duration is weakening; this tests whether strong company growth is being wrongly mapped to the physical DRAM signal.
Weak upstream pricing conflicts with strongly rising PV equities and is useful for testing company-engine versus theme-level evidence.
Gold-price earnings conversion is measurable, but commodity and valuation absorption must be separated.
Infrastructure demand supports machinery/materials, but only companies with direct earnings bridges and sound entry timing qualify.
Broad manufacturing recovery remains context rather than a narrow listed-company thesis.
